description: Static-safety lint for builder-generated files. Exposes EXACTLY: def lint(code: str, directive: dict) -> tuple[bool, list[str]] returning (is_safe, reasons). Pure function. No I/O. Imports ast and re only. Checks: (1) parse code with ast.parse; if any ast.Call.func.id == 'eval' or 'exec' AND the file uses urllib.request, requests, urlopen, or subprocess elsewhere, append reason 'eval_or_exec_with_external_input'. (2) walk ast for Call nodes where func is an Attribute with attr in {'post','put','patch'} and value.id in {'requests'} -- check the call's keyword args; if 'json' is NOT among kwarg names AND 'data' IS among them AND the directive description (from arg) mentions 'write_service' or 'WriteService' or 'JSON', append 'wrong_serialization_for_write_service'. (3) directive description contains 'PURE FUNCTION' or 'compute_score(metadata' OR phrase 'No DB writes. NO network': scan code for top-level 'while True:' loops, sockets, requests/urllib imports, subprocess imports, threading imports, signal imports -- any present means append 'pure_function_contract_violated_<which_import>'. (4) detect SQL string interpolation: any f-string or '%' formatting where the format target contains 'SELECT' or 'INSERT' or 'UPDATE' or 'DELETE' (case insensitive) -- append 'sql_string_interpolation' as warning (not blocking). is_safe = (no blocking reasons present). Returns (True, []) for clean code. NEVER raises -- all parse errors caught and returned as ('parse_error_'+exc_class). Will be wired into smoke_test_file() in zo_sentinel_builder.py as a pre-smoke gate -- NOT modified by this directive (zo_sentinel_builder.py is in PROTECTED_FILES; the wiring is a separate later directive once the lint is proven). Also include a __main__ block with at least 6 test cases: clean pure function, eval-only file, eval+http file, requests.post with data= and write_service mention, while True in a 'PURE FUNCTION' contract, SQL f-string. Print PASS/FAIL per case.
